title: Biomarkers of Paired VNS
official: Biomarkers of Paired Vagus Nerve Stimulation Therapy for Stroke Motor Rehabilitation
summary: Paired Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS) has been shown to enhance upper extremity motor recovery after ischemic stroke. Prior studies have focused primarily on long-term clinical outcomes, leaving the short-term physiologic response to the intervention poorly understood. The purpose of this study is to examine real-time responses to Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS) in individuals with chronic motor impairments after ischemic stroke to better inform Paired VNS dosing. We plan to enroll 50 participants into a single-arm study and perform neurophysiologic assessments during VNS to identify objective markers of stimulation response and examine dose-response relationships.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age ≥ 18 years old and ≤ 80 years old
2. Implanted with VNS device for post-stroke motor rehabilitation
3. Ability to follow simple commands in English

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Prior history of developmental, neurologic, or major psychiatric disorder resulting in functional disability
2. Visual or auditory disorders limiting ability to participate in study procedures
3. Evidence of an uncontrolled seizure disorder
4. Patients for whom EEG leads are contraindicated
5. Pregnancy
